liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Truckin'** (3 reviews): The Truckin' jam is called representative of what the band was doing at that time; The Truckin' > Mind Left Body > Spanish jam is subtle and empathetic rather than a psychedelic masterpiece [14][19][21]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Scarlet opener is well done; reviewer finds 1974 Scarlets a bit strange but fun [18]
- **Mississippi Half Step** (1 review): Half-Step has an unusual twist on its ending [16]
- **Row Jimmy** (1 review): Singled out, with Scarlet Begonias and China Cat, as showing the cymbal-light drumming sound [10]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): The China>Rider transition is a creative, unfamiliar take led by Jerry rather than the usual smoker [16]
- **Bertha** (1 review): Jerry's voice gives out during Bertha [18]
- **Eyes of the World** (1 review): Eyes of the World sounds warm and full [21]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Let It Grow has a strong Billy-led attack and Phil's flourishes at the climax [16]

## Setlist highlights

- **Phil and Ned**: rare: 14 archived performances [22]

## The recordings

- **gd74-07-31.sbd.ziggy.1019.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 33 songs; 233 min; rated 4.64/5 by 25 [1]. Said about its sound: Jerry's guitar sounds dreamy, and the drumming is powerful with notably few cymbals in many songs; Recording has pitch wavering through most of the first set [10][13]
- **gd1974-07-31.sbd.miller.32353.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 32 songs; 233 min; rated 4.39/5 by 41 [3]
- **gd74-07-31.degen.weiner.gdADT.7363.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 30 songs; 190 min; rated 3.47/5 by 17 [9]. Said about its sound: Audience tape has talkers during China Doll and quiet parts, loud sneezes, clumsy editing, and missing opening songs [17]
- **gd1974-07-31.sbd.matera.112951.flac16**: soundboard; 34 songs; 231 min [2]

## Around the show

- Three sets were rare in 1974 (compare 2/22 and 6/16); reviewer thinks this show deserves a top spot [12]
- Reviewer ranks this with 7/19/74 as favorites among strong summer 1974 shows [14]
- Compared with many post-1972 pre-hiatus shows, it has a solid setlist, diligent jamming and no dead spots [19]
- Reviewer considers the show underrated and mentions a good soundboard available on GDlive [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd74-07-31.sbd.ziggy.1019.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]
- **gd1974-07-31.sbd.miller.32353.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel (7inch @ 7.5ips 1/2 Track) -> Dat -> CD D [3]. Also: Cleaned-up, patched version of shnid 1019, with Bill Degen's audience tape filling Row Jimmy reel flip and Weather Report Suite intro; Source chain: unknown mics, master cassette, 7-inch reel, DAT, then SHN; start of Scarlet is cut [3]
- **gd74-07-31.degen.weiner.gdADT.7363.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Bill Degen; source: Audience Recording [9]
- **gd1974-07-31.sbd.matera.112951.flac16**: transferred by Phil Matera**; source: The baseline used for this release: gd1974-07-31.1019 (SBDMR> DATx> CD> DAT> CD> EAC> SHN) I used Cool Edit 2000 to perform amplitude and EQ adjustments. EQ… [2]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Dillon Stadium - July 31, 1974](https://www.dead.net/show/july-31-1974) [23]
- Poster by Worthpoint: [Grateful Dead Dave's Picks Vol 2 - Dillon Stadium, Hartford CT - 7/31/74 - MINT | #4657860572](https://www.worthpoint.com/worthopedia/grateful-dead-daves-picks-vol-dillon-4657860572) [24]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Dillon Stadium - July 31, 1974](https://www.dead.net/show/july-31-1974) [25]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Dillon Stadium - July 31, 1974](https://www.dead.net/show/july-31-1974) [26]
- Fan art by RareVinyl.com: [Grateful Dead Dave's Picks Volume 2: Dillon Stadium, Hartford, CT 7/31/74 US 3-CD set](https://us.rarevinyl.com/products/grateful-dead-dave-s-picks-volume-2-dillon-stadium-hartford-ct-7-31-74-us-3-cd-album-triple-set-r2529204-848360) [27]
- Poster by Steve Caraway Grateful Dead: [1974-07-31 Dillon Stadium, Hartford, CT, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1974-07-31-dillon-stadium-hartford-ct-usa/) [28]
